name: How Long Does a Tub-to-Shower Conversion Really Take?

step.name: Step 1
step.text: If you're considering swapping out your old tub for a sleek new shower, you're probably wondering about the timeline. While every project is unique, a full bathroom remodel that includes a barrier-free shower typically takes about 2 to 3 weeks from start to finish. This isn't just about quick demolition and installation; there are some crucial steps that need their own time. Phase 1: Planning and Demolition. This is where we remove the old tub, and any necessary subfloor modifications for proper drainage happen. This initial phase can take a few days, depending on the complexity of your existing setup. Phase 2: Structural and Plumbing Adjustments. If we need to move plumbing or make significant changes to your subfloor, this phase will take a bit longer. It's all about ensuring the foundation for your new shower is solid and leak-proof. Phase 3: Waterproofing and Tile Installation. This is where patience is key! Waterproofing membranes need proper drying time to be effective, and detailed tile work is essential for both aesthetics and function. This phase often takes the longest to ensure everything is perfect. Phase 4: Fixture Installation and Finishing Touches. Once the tile is set and cured, we install your shower fixtures, glass enclosures, and complete any final painting or trim. Keep in mind that structural complexity or unexpected plumbing upgrades can sometimes extend the schedule. We always aim for clear communication throughout the process so you know what to expect.
